fullPassage: Located in the historic city of Ningbo (in Zhejiang province), China, the Ningbo Museum is a testament to the culture of the city. The museum, designed by Chinese architect Wang Shu, is a symbol of a deceased civilization and the geographical features of the city. Completed in 2008, the museum combines contemporary design and historical context, smoothly blending into the surrounding landscape. The museum's outside is largely composed of debris collected from the area, where traditional villages were destroyed to make way for new developments. In the building of the museum, Wang Shu used a traditional Chinese construction method called 'wapan,' demonstrating his deep respect for cultural heritage and eco-friendly design. Wapan referred to a technique of recycling used materials, especially old bricks saved from destroyed buildings, in the construction process. Wang Shu's skillful use of wapan results in a unique frontage that tells a story of preservation and continuation. Inside the museum, visitors are welcomed by an impressive collection of artifacts and displays, carefully organized to describe the story of Ningbo's lively history. The Ningbo History Museum stands not only as a cultural point of interest but also as proof of Wang Shu's forward-thinking approach, respecting the past while impacting the future of architecture in China. The Church of the Light, designed by Japanese architect Tadao Ando, is an impressive architectural masterpiece in Osaka and that inspires deep thought and spiritual peace. This exceptional building, completed in 1989 expresses Ando's distinct style — simplicity and innovative use of natural light. With its concrete walls and unique cross-shaped opening, the structure invites people to experience an ever-changing interplay between light and dark as it creates a calm, reflective atmosphere within its sacred walls. With this design, Ando cleverly illuminates the architectural idea of "engawa" to create a special spatial experience. Engawa, a traditional element of Japanese architecture, refers to a narrow strip of flooring that forms a middle ground between indoor and outdoor spaces. Ando applies this concept by adding an engawa-like feature — a thin slit between the concrete walls and the church's roof. This narrow opening, located where the walls meet, allows a gentle flow of natural light to enter the interior and softly illuminate the area around the altar. The engawa does more than just create a path for light — it also acts as a meaningful boundary separating the everyday world outside from the sacred area inside. This careful integration of engawa in the Church of the Light's design shows Ando's talent for combining traditional principles of Japanese architecte with a modern perspective, ultimately creating a peaceful atmosphere for worshipers and visitors alike. The Seoul Arts Center, a multi-cultural art complex located in Seoul, stands as a symbol of Korea's artistic expression. Spreading across a large campus at the foot of a mountain, this complex is a center for various art forms, from music and dance to theater and visual arts. Whether it's hosting art performances, exhibitions, or learning programs, it represents the country's artistic heritage and promotes the enjoyment of different artistic mediums. The Seoul Arts Center was a national project by the Korean government, which was started to promote the country's artistic excellence, in preparation for the hosting of the 1988 Olympics. Designed by architect Kim Seokchul with the idea of traditional Korean spirit and culture, the Music Hall was first completed in 1988. The building has a shape of a Korean traditional fan buchae when seen from above. Later in 1993, the Opera House was completed with an outer design that looks like a gat, a Korean traditional hat. Both buchae and gat are said to symbolize the classical scholar and taste in Korean culture. Besides, the roof's edges are designed like the hanging edges of a traditional Korean house. At first, the Opera House was criticized for being poorly designed. However, seen as a valuable asset to the future cultural heritage of Seoul, the Seoul Arts Center was selected in 2013 as "Seoul Future Heritage" by Seoul City. In these East Asian architectural wonders, we witness not only the smooth blending of ancient wisdom into modern looks but also the commitment of forward-thinking architects to respecting their cultural heritage. These structures stand not just as buildings but as symbols of deep respect for tradition and innovation. It also reminds us that architecture can connect history to our own lives and make a lasting impact on human imagination. As East Asia keeps growing and changing, its architecture will surely remain a lively reflection of the area's rich history and promising future.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: the Opera House was ___ 는 오페라하우스가 '완공되었다'라는 수동태(be동사 was + 과거분사)이다. complete의 과거분사는 completed이므로 was completed가 맞다.
det.tip: 수동태 be + p.p.: was completed(완공되었다)

questions.passage: __________ (spread) across a large campus at the foot of a mountain, this complex is a center for various art forms, from music and dance to theater and visual arts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: 콤마 앞부분은 주어 this complex를 의미상 주어로 하는 분사구문이다. 단지가 캠퍼스에 '펼쳐져 있는' 능동·진행의 의미이므로 현재분사 Spreading이 맞다.
det.tip: 문장 앞 분사구문: 능동 의미이면 현재분사(Spreading ~, this complex is ...)

questions.passage: Located in the historic city of Ningbo (in Zhejiang province), China, the Ningbo Museum is a testament to the culture of the city. The museum, designed by Chinese architect Wang Shu, is a symbol of a deceased civilization and the geographical features of the city. Completed in 2008, the museum combines contemporary design and historical context, smoothly blending into the surrounding landscape. The museum's outside is largely composed of debris collected from the area, where traditional villages were destroyed to __________ for new developments. In the building of the museum, Wang Shu used a traditional Chinese construction method called 'wapan,' demonstrating his deep respect for cultural heritage and eco-friendly design.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① take turns: 번갈아 하다 부적합
❌ ② keep pace: 보조를 맞추다 부적합
❌ ③ stand still: 가만히 서 있다 부적합
✅ ④ make way: 전통 마을이 헐린 것은 새 개발에 '자리를 내주기' 위해서 ← 정답
det.tip: make way for = ~에게 자리를 내주다, 길을 터 주다

questions.passage: With this design, Ando cleverly illuminates the architectural idea of "engawa" to create a special spatial experience. Engawa, a traditional element of Japanese architecture, refers to a narrow strip of flooring that forms a __________ between indoor and outdoor spaces. Ando applies this concept by adding an engawa-like feature — a thin slit between the concrete walls and the church's roof. This narrow opening, located where the walls meet, allows a gentle flow of natural light to enter the interior and softly illuminate the area around the altar. The engawa does more than just create a path for light — it also acts as a meaningful boundary separating the everyday world outside from the sacred area inside.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① final destination: 최종 목적지 부적합
❌ ② hidden treasure: 숨겨진 보물 부적합
✅ ③ middle ground: 실내와 실외 '사이(between indoor and outdoor spaces)'에 형성되는 좁은 마루이므로 '중간 지대' ← 정답
❌ ④ common sense: 상식 부적합
det.tip: between indoor and outdoor spaces(실내외 사이)가 단서 — 중간 지대(middle ground)
